Puteri Saadong and the Journey of Sacrifice
In the rich historical landscape of Kelantan, one name stands out as a symbol of grace,
wisdom, and sacrifice—Puteri Saadong. She was the daughter of Raja Loyor of Jembal and the
adopted heir of the legendary queen, Che Siti Wan Kembang Ralsed within the royal court, she
was well-educated in state affairs, traditional healing, and the arts. Upon reaching maturity, she
married Raja Abdullah and ascended as queen. 27
Under their rule, Kelantan flourished economically and culturally. 28
Viewing Kelantan as a potential threat, the Siamese king demanded regular tribule as a sign of
submission. Raja Abdullah, confident in his sovereignty, refused to comply. This defiance
provoked the Slamese kingdom,which responded by launching a military campaign against
Kelantan, eventually capluring Raja Abdullah in the conflict.
Faced with the potential collapse of her kingdom and the imprisonment of her husband,
Puteri Saadong made a profoundly courageous decision. 29
Her decision was
not born of fear but of strategic foresight. She recognised that personal sacrifice might prevent
greater suffering and preserve the dignity of Kelantan. The Siamese king welcomed her,
captivated by her intelligence and composure.
During her time in the Siamese palace, Puteri Saadong remained composed and
principled. 30
As fate would have it, the Siamese king fell gravely ill. His physicians
failed to restore his health, and the court fell into despair. Puterl Saadong, skilled in traditional
Malay medicine, offered her assistance. Applying her knowledge with care and precision, she
gradually nursed the king back to health. His recoverynot only reaffirmed her slatus but also
soflened his stance toward Kelantan.

permitted her to relurn home. Upon her arrival in Kelantan, she resumed her duties with quiet
strength.
She continued to rule from Kola Jelasin, focusing on rebuilding
and maintaining peace. Her return symbolised not only the resilience of her spirit but also the
endurance of her people.
In the later years of her life, Puteri Saadong withdrew from active rule and sought spiritual
retreat. She relocated to Bukit Marak, a place where she offered healing and counsel to the local
community. Eventually, she journeyed 1o Gunung Ayam, a sacred mountain associated with
mysticism and seclusion. It is said that she disappeared there, leaving no trace. 32.
Today, Puteri Saadong is remembered not only as a historical figure but also as a cultural
icon. Her life illustrates the complexity of leadership, the strength of personal conviction and the
depth of love for one's homeland. From the halls of Kota Jelasin to the quiet slopes of Gunung
Ayam,her journey reflects the endunng values of sacrifice, wisdom and national pride. Her story
continues to inspire generations, reminding us that true leadership is often defined not by power,
but by selflessness and courage in the face of adversity.
